1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# tools/check-round-independence.sh: is an interview transcript asked in
     4	# prerequisite-ordered rounds?
     5	#
     6	# In `interview.pacing: rounds` every round of questions ends with one comment
     7	# block (discovering-requirements/resources/REFERENCE.md §Question Pacing):
     8	#
     9	#   <!-- round: 2; questions: [{"id":"Q4","depends_on":[]},{"id":"Q2","depends_on":[],"reasked":true}] -->
    10	#
    11	# This checker reads those blocks from a transcript (markdown or plain text,
    12	# one block per line) and fails when:
    13	#   * a `depends_on` names a question asked in the same round,
    14	#   * a `depends_on` names a question not asked in an earlier round,
    15	#   * a non-reasked id repeats, or a `reasked` id was never asked before,
    16	#   * round numbers do not increase, or a block is malformed,
    17	#   * the rounds average fewer than --min-average new questions (default 2).
    18	# `reasked` entries are skipped for id uniqueness and for the average. The
    19	# final round is exempt from the average when there are two or more rounds.
    20	#
    21	# Usage:
    22	#   tools/check-round-independence.sh <transcript> [--min-average N] [--json]
    23	#
    24	# Exit codes: 0 independent · 1 violation · 2 usage, unreadable file, or no
    25	#             round block in the transcript
    26	# =============================================================================
    27	set -euo pipefail
    28	export LC_ALL=C
    29	
    30	usage() { sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# Exit codes/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; }
    31	
    32	TRANSCRIPT=""
    33	MIN_AVG="2"
    34	JSON=0
    35	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    36	  case "$1" in
    37	    --min-average)
    38	      [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || { echo "check-round-independence.sh: --min-average needs a number" >&2; exit 2; }
    39	      MIN_AVG="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    40	    --json) JSON=1; shift ;;
    41	    --help|-h) usage; exit 0 ;;
    42	    --) shift; [[ $# -ge 1 ]] && { TRANSCRIPT="$1"; shift; } ;;
    43	    -*) echo "check-round-independence.sh: unknown flag $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    44	    *)
    45	      [[ -z "$TRANSCRIPT" ]] || { echo "check-round-independence.sh: one transcript only" >&2; exit 2; }
    46	      TRANSCRIPT="$1"; shift ;;
    47	  esac
    48	done
    49	
    50	[[ -n "$TRANSCRIPT" ]] || { echo "check-round-independence.sh: transcript path required" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2; }
    51	[[ -f "$TRANSCRIPT" && -r "$TRANSCRIPT" ]] || { echo "check-round-independence.sh: cannot read $TRANSCRIPT" >&2; exit 2; }
    52	[[ "$MIN_AVG" =~ ^[0-9]+([.][0-9]+)?$ ]] || { echo "check-round-independence.sh: --min-average must be a non-negative number, got '$MIN_AVG'" >&2; exit 2; }
    53	command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "check-round-independence.sh: jq is required" >&2; exit 2; }
    54	
    55	BLOCK_RE='<!--[[:space:]]*round:[[:space:]]*[0-9]+[[:space:]]*;[[:space:]]*questions:[[:space:]]*\[.*\][[:space:]]*-->'
    56	
    57	# One JSON object per block: {round, questions} or {round, malformed}. grep exits
    58	# 1 on no match, which is the "no block" case below, not an error.
    59	blocks="$(grep -oE "$BLOCK_RE" "$TRANSCRIPT" || true)"
    60	if [[ -z "$blocks" ]]; then
    61	  echo "check-round-independence.sh: no <!-- round: N; questions: [...] --> block in $TRANSCRIPT" >&2
    62	  exit 2
    63	fi
    64	
    65	rounds_json="[]"
    66	while IFS= read -r block; do
    67	  [[ -n "$block" ]] || continue
    68	  n="$(printf '%s\n' "$block" | sed -E 's/^<!--[[:space:]]*round:[[:space:]]*([0-9]+).*/\1/')"
    69	  [[ ${#n} -le 9 ]] || { echo "check-round-independence.sh: round number $n is too long" >&2; exit 1; }
    70	  n=$((10#$n))   # "02" is not valid JSON; the round number is decimal
    71	  arr="$(printf '%s\n' "$block" | sed -E 's/^<!--[[:space:]]*round:[[:space:]]*[0-9]+[[:space:]]*;[[:space:]]*questions:[[:space:]]*//; s/[[:space:]]*-->$//')"
    72	  if printf '%s' "$arr" | jq -e 'type == "array" and all(.[];
    73	        type == "object" and (.id | type == "string" and length > 0)
    74	        and (.depends_on | type == "array" and all(.[]; type == "string")))' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    75	    entry="$(jq -cn --argjson r "$n" --argjson q "$arr" '{round: $r, questions: $q}')"
    76	  else
    77	    entry="$(jq -cn --argjson r "$n" --arg raw "$arr" '{round: $r, malformed: $raw}')"
    78	  fi
    79	  rounds_json="$(jq -cn --argjson a "$rounds_json" --argjson e "$entry" '$a + [$e]')"
    80	done <<< "$blocks"
    81	
    82	report="$(jq -n --argjson rounds "$rounds_json" --argjson min "$MIN_AVG" '
    83	  reduce range(0; $rounds | length) as $i (
    84	    {asked: [], violations: [], per_round: [], prev: null};
    85	    $rounds[$i] as $r
    86	    | (if .prev != null and $r.round <= .prev
    87	         then .violations += ["round \($r.round) does not follow round \(.prev)"] else . end)
    88	    | .prev = $r.round
    89	    | if $r.malformed != null then
    90	        .violations += ["round \($r.round): malformed questions array (each entry needs a string id and a depends_on array of strings)"]
    91	        | .per_round += [{round: $r.round, new: 0, reasked: 0, ids: []}]
    92	      else
    93	        ($r.questions | map(.id)) as $here
    94	        | .asked as $before
    95	        | reduce $r.questions[] as $q (.;
    96	            ($q.reasked == true) as $re
    97	            | (if $re then
    98	                 (if ($before | index([$q.id])) == null
    99	                    then .violations += ["round \($r.round): \($q.id) is marked reasked but was not asked in an earlier round"] else . end)
   100	               else
   101	                 (if (.asked | index([$q.id])) != null
   102	                    then .violations += ["round \($r.round): \($q.id) is asked again without \"reasked\": true"] else . end)
   103	                 | .asked += [$q.id]
   104	               end)
   105	            | reduce $q.depends_on[] as $d (.;
   106	                if ($here | index([$d])) != null and $d != $q.id then
   107	                  .violations += ["round \($r.round): \($q.id) depends on \($d), asked in the same round"]
   108	                elif $d == $q.id then
   109	                  .violations += ["round \($r.round): \($q.id) depends on itself"]
   110	                elif ($before | index([$d])) == null then
   111	                  .violations += ["round \($r.round): \($q.id) depends on \($d), not asked in an earlier round"]
   112	                else . end))
   113	        | .per_round += [{
   114	            round: $r.round,
   115	            new: ($r.questions | map(select(.reasked != true)) | length),
   116	            reasked: ($r.questions | map(select(.reasked == true)) | length),
   117	            ids: $here }]
   118	      end)
   119	  | .counted = (if (.per_round | length) >= 2 then .per_round[0:-1] else .per_round end)
   120	  | .average = (if (.counted | length) == 0 then 0
   121	                else ((.counted | map(.new) | add) / (.counted | length)) end)
   122	  | (if .average < $min
   123	       then .violations += ["average \(.average * 100 | round / 100) new questions per round is below --min-average \($min)"] else . end)
   124	  | {
   125	      rounds: (.per_round | length),
   126	      questions: (.per_round | map(.new) | add),
   127	      reasked: (.per_round | map(.reasked) | add),
   128	      average: (.average * 100 | round / 100),
   129	      min_average: $min,
   130	      final_round_exempt: ((.per_round | length) >= 2),
   131	      per_round: .per_round,
   132	      violations: .violations,
   133	      verdict: (if (.violations | length) == 0 then "PASS" else "FAIL" end)
   134	    }')"
   135	
   136	if [[ "$JSON" -eq 1 ]]; then
   137	  printf '%s\n' "$report"
   138	else
   139	  printf '%s\n' "$report" | jq -r '
   140	    (.per_round[] | "round \(.round): \(.new) new question(s)\(if .reasked > 0 then ", \(.reasked) re-asked" else "" end) [\(.ids | join(" "))]"),
   141	    "rounds: \(.rounds); questions: \(.questions); average: \(.average) per round\(if .final_round_exempt then " (final round exempt)" else "" end); min-average: \(.min_average)",
   142	    (.violations[] | "VIOLATION: \(.)"),
   143	    .verdict'
   144	fi
   145	
   146	verdict="$(printf '%s\n' "$report" | jq -r '.verdict')"
   147	[[ "$verdict" == "PASS" ]]

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# tools/check-round-independence.sh: is an interview transcript asked in
     4	# prerequisite-ordered rounds?
     5	#
     6	# In `interview.pacing: rounds` every round of questions ends with one comment
     7	# block (discovering-requirements/resources/REFERENCE.md §Question Pacing):
     8	#
     9	#   <!-- round: 2; questions: [{"id":"Q4","depends_on":[]},{"id":"Q2","depends_on":[],"reasked":true}] -->
    10	#
    11	# This checker reads those blocks from a transcript (markdown or plain text,
    12	# one block per line) and fails when:
    13	#   * a `depends_on` names a question asked in the same round,
    14	#   * a `depends_on` names a question not asked in an earlier round,
    15	#   * a non-reasked id repeats, or a `reasked` id was never asked before,
    16	#   * round numbers do not increase, or a block is malformed,
    17	#   * the rounds average fewer than --min-average new questions (default 2).
    18	# `reasked` entries are skipped for id uniqueness and for the average. The
    19	# final round is exempt from the average when there are two or more rounds.
    20	#
    21	# Usage:
    22	#   tools/check-round-independence.sh <transcript> [--min-average N] [--json]
    23	#
    24	# Exit codes: 0 independent · 1 violation · 2 usage, unreadable file, or no
    25	#             round block in the transcript
    26	# =============================================================================
    27	set -euo pipefail
    28	export LC_ALL=C
    29	
    30	usage() { sed -n '/^# Usage:/,/^# Exit codes/p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; }
    31	
    32	TRANSCRIPT=""
    33	MIN_AVG="2"
    34	JSON=0
    35	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    36	  case "$1" in
    37	    --min-average)
    38	      [[ $# -ge 2 ]] || { echo "check-round-independence.sh: --min-average needs a number" >&2; exit 2; }
    39	      MIN_AVG="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    40	    --json) JSON=1; shift ;;
    41	    --help|-h) usage; exit 0 ;;
    42	    --) shift; [[ $# -ge 1 ]] && { TRANSCRIPT="$1"; shift; } ;;
    43	    -*) echo "check-round-independence.sh: unknown flag $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
    44	    *)
    45	      [[ -z "$TRANSCRIPT" ]] || { echo "check-round-independence.sh: one transcript only" >&2; exit 2; }
    46	      TRANSCRIPT="$1"; shift ;;
    47	  esac
    48	done
    49	
    50	[[ -n "$TRANSCRIPT" ]] || { echo "check-round-independence.sh: transcript path required" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2; }
    51	[[ -f "$TRANSCRIPT" && -r "$TRANSCRIPT" ]] || { echo "check-round-independence.sh: cannot read $TRANSCRIPT" >&2; exit 2; }
    52	[[ "$MIN_AVG" =~ ^[0-9]+([.][0-9]+)?$ ]] || { echo "check-round-independence.sh: --min-average must be a non-negative number, got '$MIN_AVG'" >&2; exit 2; }
    53	command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "check-round-independence.sh: jq is required" >&2; exit 2; }
    54	
    55	BLOCK_RE='<!--[[:space:]]*round:[[:space:]]*[0-9]+[[:space:]]*;[[:space:]]*questions:[[:space:]]*\[.*\][[:space:]]*-->'
    56	
    57	# One JSON object per block: {round, questions} or {round, malformed}. grep exits
    58	# 1 on no match, which is the "no block" case below, not an error.
    59	blocks="$(grep -oE "$BLOCK_RE" "$TRANSCRIPT" || true)"
    60	if [[ -z "$blocks" ]]; then
    61	  echo "check-round-independence.sh: no <!-- round: N; questions: [...] --> block in $TRANSCRIPT" >&2
    62	  exit 2
    63	fi
    64	
    65	rounds_json="[]"
    66	while IFS= read -r block; do
    67	  [[ -n "$block" ]] || continue
    68	  n="$(printf '%s\n' "$block" | sed -E 's/^<!--[[:space:]]*round:[[:space:]]*([0-9]+).*/\1/')"
    69	  [[ ${#n} -le 9 ]] || { echo "check-round-independence.sh: round number $n is too long" >&2; exit 1; }
    70	  n=$((10#$n))   # "02" is not valid JSON; the round number is decimal
    71	  arr="$(printf '%s\n' "$block" | sed -E 's/^<!--[[:space:]]*round:[[:space:]]*[0-9]+[[:space:]]*;[[:space:]]*questions:[[:space:]]*//; s/[[:space:]]*-->$//')"
    72	  if printf '%s' "$arr" | jq -e 'type == "array" and all(.[];
    73	        type == "object" and (.id | type == "string" and length > 0)
    74	        and (.depends_on | type == "array" and all(.[]; type == "string")))' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    75	    entry="$(jq -cn --argjson r "$n" --argjson q "$arr" '{round: $r, questions: $q}')"
    76	  else
    77	    entry="$(jq -cn --argjson r "$n" --arg raw "$arr" '{round: $r, malformed: $raw}')"
    78	  fi
    79	  rounds_json="$(jq -cn --argjson a "$rounds_json" --argjson e "$entry" '$a + [$e]')"
    80	done <<< "$blocks"
    81	
    82	report="$(jq -n --argjson rounds "$rounds_json" --argjson min "$MIN_AVG" '
    83	  reduce range(0; $rounds | length) as $i (
    84	    {asked: [], violations: [], per_round: [], prev: null};
    85	    $rounds[$i] as $r
    86	    | (if .prev != null and $r.round <= .prev
    87	         then .violations += ["round \($r.round) does not follow round \(.prev)"] else . end)
    88	    | .prev = $r.round
    89	    | if $r.malformed != null then
    90	        .violations += ["round \($r.round): malformed questions array (each entry needs a string id and a depends_on array of strings)"]
    91	        | .per_round += [{round: $r.round, new: 0, reasked: 0, ids: []}]
    92	      else
    93	        ($r.questions | map(.id)) as $here
    94	        | .asked as $before
    95	        | reduce $r.questions[] as $q (.;
    96	            ($q.reasked == true) as $re
    97	            | (if $re then
    98	                 (if ($before | index([$q.id])) == null
    99	                    then .violations += ["round \($r.round): \($q.id) is marked reasked but was not asked in an earlier round"] else . end)
   100	               else
   101	                 (if (.asked | index([$q.id])) != null
   102	                    then .violations += ["round \($r.round): \($q.id) is asked again without \"reasked\": true"] else . end)
   103	                 | .asked += [$q.id]
   104	               end)
   105	            | reduce $q.depends_on[] as $d (.;
   106	                if ($here | index([$d])) != null and $d != $q.id then
   107	                  .violations += ["round \($r.round): \($q.id) depends on \($d), asked in the same round"]
   108	                elif $d == $q.id then
   109	                  .violations += ["round \($r.round): \($q.id) depends on itself"]
   110	                elif ($before | index([$d])) == null then
   111	                  .violations += ["round \($r.round): \($q.id) depends on \($d), not asked in an earlier round"]
   112	                else . end))
   113	        | .per_round += [{
   114	            round: $r.round,
   115	            new: ($r.questions | map(select(.reasked != true)) | length),
   116	            reasked: ($r.questions | map(select(.reasked == true)) | length),
   117	            ids: $here }]
   118	      end)
   119	  | .counted = (if (.per_round | length) >= 2 then .per_round[0:-1] else .per_round end)
   120	  | .average = (if (.counted | length) == 0 then 0
   121	                else ((.counted | map(.new) | add) / (.counted | length)) end)
   122	  | (if .average < $min
   123	       then .violations += ["average \(.average * 100 | round / 100) new questions per round is below --min-average \($min)"] else . end)
   124	  | {
   125	      rounds: (.per_round | length),
   126	      questions: (.per_round | map(.new) | add),
   127	      reasked: (.per_round | map(.reasked) | add),
   128	      average: (.average * 100 | round / 100),
   129	      min_average: $min,
   130	      final_round_exempt: ((.per_round | length) >= 2),
   131	      per_round: .per_round,
   132	      violations: .violations,
   133	      verdict: (if (.violations | length) == 0 then "PASS" else "FAIL" end)
   134	    }')"
   135	
   136	if [[ "$JSON" -eq 1 ]]; then
   137	  printf '%s\n' "$report"
   138	else
   139	  printf '%s\n' "$report" | jq -r '
   140	    (.per_round[] | "round \(.round): \(.new) new question(s)\(if .reasked > 0 then ", \(.reasked) re-asked" else "" end) [\(.ids | join(" "))]"),
   141	    "rounds: \(.rounds); questions: \(.questions); average: \(.average) per round\(if .final_round_exempt then " (final round exempt)" else "" end); min-average: \(.min_average)",
   142	    (.violations[] | "VIOLATION: \(.)"),
   143	    .verdict'
   144	fi
   145	
   146	verdict="$(printf '%s\n' "$report" | jq -r '.verdict')"
   147	[[ "$verdict" == "PASS" ]]

     5

    10	➡ Recommended: yes

    12	❓ Q2: Write access

    14	➡ Recommended: yes

1	#!/usr/bin/env bats
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# tests/unit/check-round-independence.bats
     4	#
     5	# tools/check-round-independence.sh reads the `<!-- round: N; questions: [...] -->`
     6	# blocks that `interview.pacing: rounds` puts at the end of every round
     7	# (discovering-requirements/resources/REFERENCE.md §Question Pacing) and fails
     8	# when a question depends on another question of the same round, on one never
     9	# asked earlier, when ids repeat without "reasked", or when rounds average
    10	# fewer than --min-average new questions (final round exempt).
    11	# =============================================================================
    12	
    13	setup() {
    14	    SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
    15	    PROJECT_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
    16	    CHECK="$PROJECT_ROOT/tools/check-round-independence.sh"
    17	    FIX="$PROJECT_ROOT/tests/fixtures/rounds"
    18	    T="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/transcript.md"
    19	}
    20	
    21	# Write a transcript whose rounds are the given JSON arrays, in order.
    22	transcript() {
    23	    local n=0 arr
    24	    : > "$T"
    25	    for arr in "$@"; do
    26	        n=$((n + 1))
    27	        printf 'Round %d\n\nquestions...\n<!-- round: %d; questions: %s -->\n\n' "$n" "$n" "$arr" >> "$T"
    28	    done
    29	}
    30	
    31	@test "RI-1 the independent fixture passes at the default minimum and reports per-round counts" {
    32	    run "$CHECK" "$FIX/independent.md"
    33	    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    34	    [[ "$output" == *"round 1: 3 new question(s) [Q1 Q2 Q3]"* ]]
    35	    [[ "$output" == *"round 3: 1 new question(s), 1 re-asked [Q6 Q7]"* ]]
    36	    [[ "$output" == *"rounds: 4; questions: 8; average: 2.33 per round (final round exempt); min-average: 2"* ]]
    37	    [[ "$output" == *"PASS"* ]]
    38	}
    39	
    40	@test "RI-2 the fixture has at least three rounds and --json carries the report fields" {
    41	    run "$CHECK" "$FIX/independent.md" --json
    42	    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    43	    [ "$(jq -r '.rounds' <<< "$output")" -ge 3 ]
    44	    [ "$(jq -r '.verdict' <<< "$output")" = "PASS" ]
    45	    [ "$(jq -r '.min_average' <<< "$output")" = "2" ]
    46	    [ "$(jq -r '.final_round_exempt' <<< "$output")" = "true" ]
    47	    [ "$(jq -r '.violations | length' <<< "$output")" -eq 0 ]
    48	    [ "$(jq -r '.per_round | length' <<< "$output")" -eq "$(jq -r '.rounds' <<< "$output")" ]
    49	}
    50	
    51	@test "RI-3 the negative fixture fails on its same-round dependency" {
    52	    run "$CHECK" "$FIX/same-round-dependency.md"
    53	    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
    54	    [[ "$output" == *"VIOLATION: round 1: Q3 depends on Q2, asked in the same round"* ]]
    55	    [[ "$output" == *"FAIL"* ]]

    61	               '[{"id":"Q5","depends_on":["Q3"]}]'
    62	    run "$CHECK" "$T" --json
    63	    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    64	    [ "$(jq -r '.average' <<< "$output")" = "2" ]
    65	}
    66	
    67	@test "RI-5 a one-question round that is not the final round fails the default minimum" {

    69	               '[{"id":"Q2","depends_on":["Q1"]}]' \
    70	               '[{"id":"Q3","depends_on":["Q2"]}]'

    72	    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
    73	    [[ "$output" == *"below --min-average 2"* ]]

    75	    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    76	}
    77	
    78	@test "RI-6 a single round is held to the minimum (no exemption with one round)" {
    79	    transcript '[{"id":"Q1","depends_on":[]}]'
    80	    run "$CHECK" "$T" --json
    81	    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
    82	    [ "$(jq -r '.final_round_exempt' <<< "$output")" = "false" ]
    83	}
    84	
    85	@test "RI-7 reasked entries are ignored for uniqueness and the average" {
    86	    transcript '[{"id":"Q1","depends_on":[]},{"id":"Q2","depends_on":[]}]' \
    87	               '[{"id":"Q2","depends_on":[],"reasked":true},{"id":"Q3","depends_on":["Q1"]},{"id":"Q4","depends_on":[]}]' \
    88	               '[{"id":"Q5","depends_on":["Q2"]}]'
    89	    run "$CHECK" "$T" --json
    90	    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
    91	    [ "$(jq -r '.questions' <<< "$output")" = "5" ]
    92	    [ "$(jq -r '.reasked' <<< "$output")" = "1" ]
    93	    [ "$(jq -r '.average' <<< "$output")" = "2" ]
    94	}
    95	
    96	@test "RI-8 a repeated id without reasked fails; reasked on a never-asked id fails" {
    97	    transcript '[{"id":"Q1","depends_on":[]},{"id":"Q2","depends_on":[]}]' \
    98	               '[{"id":"Q2","depends_on":[]},{"id":"Q3","depends_on":[]}]'
    99	    run "$CHECK" "$T"
   100	    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
   101	    [[ "$output" == *'Q2 is asked again without "reasked": true'* ]]
   102	    transcript '[{"id":"Q1","depends_on":[]},{"id":"Q2","depends_on":[]}]' \
   103	               '[{"id":"Q9","depends_on":[],"reasked":true},{"id":"Q3","depends_on":[]}]'
   104	    run "$CHECK" "$T"
   105	    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
   106	    [[ "$output" == *"Q9 is marked reasked but was not asked in an earlier round"* ]]
   107	}
   108	
   109	@test "RI-9 a dependency on an unknown or later question fails" {
   110	    transcript '[{"id":"Q1","depends_on":["Q7"]},{"id":"Q2","depends_on":[]}]' \
   111	               '[{"id":"Q7","depends_on":[]},{"id":"Q3","depends_on":[]}]'
   112	    run "$CHECK" "$T"
   113	    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
   114	    [[ "$output" == *"round 1: Q1 depends on Q7, not asked in an earlier round"* ]]
   115	}
   116	
   117	@test "RI-10 a self-dependency and a non-increasing round number fail" {
   118	    transcript '[{"id":"Q1","depends_on":["Q1"]},{"id":"Q2","depends_on":[]}]'
   119	    run "$CHECK" "$T"
   120	    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
   121	    [[ "$output" == *"Q1 depends on itself"* ]]
   122	    printf '%s\n' '<!-- round: 2; questions: [{"id":"Q1","depends_on":[]},{"id":"Q2","depends_on":[]}] -->' \
   123	                  '<!-- round: 1; questions: [{"id":"Q3","depends_on":[]},{"id":"Q4","depends_on":[]}] -->' > "$T"
   124	    run "$CHECK" "$T"
   125	    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
   126	    [[ "$output" == *"round 1 does not follow round 2"* ]]
   127	}
   128	
   129	@test "RI-11 a malformed questions array is a violation, not a crash" {
   130	    printf '%s\n' '<!-- round: 1; questions: [{"id":"Q1"},{"id":"Q2","depends_on":"Q1"}] -->' \
   131	                  '<!-- round: 2; questions: [not json] -->' > "$T"
   132	    run "$CHECK" "$T"
   133	    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
   134	    [[ "$output" == *"round 1: malformed questions array"* ]]
   135	    [[ "$output" == *"round 2: malformed questions array"* ]]
   136	}
   137	
   138	@test "RI-12 no round block exits 2; usage errors exit 2" {
   139	    printf 'an interview with no round blocks\n' > "$T"
   140	    run "$CHECK" "$T"
   141	    [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
   142	    [[ "$output" == *"no <!-- round: N; questions: [...] --> block"* ]]
   143	    run "$CHECK"
   144	    [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
   145	    run "$CHECK" "$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/missing.md"
   146	    [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
   147	    run "$CHECK" "$FIX/independent.md" --min-average two
   148	    [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
   149	    run "$CHECK" "$FIX/independent.md" --bogus
   150	    [ "$status" -eq 2 ]
   151	}
   152	
   153	@test "RI-13 the REFERENCE.md worked example is itself a valid round" {
   154	    local ref="$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/skills/discovering-requirements/resources/REFERENCE.md"
   155	    {
   156	        printf '%s\n' '<!-- round: 1; questions: [{"id":"Q1","depends_on":[]},{"id":"Q2","depends_on":[]},{"id":"Q3","depends_on":[]}] -->'
   157	        grep -E '^<!-- round: 2;' "$ref"
   158	    } > "$T"
   159	    [ "$(grep -c '^<!-- round: 2;' "$T")" -eq 1 ]

#!/usr/bin/env bats
# =============================================================================
# dec-write-lib.bats: the decision-ledger writer (.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh).
#
# Hermetic: every test copies the writer, its validator and compat-lib into a fresh temp project
# (its own git repo and .run), so the host's run state, the live ledger and the operator's session
# never leak in. The live grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml of this repository is never written.
# Seams: the CLI (subcommands, exit codes) and the ledger file after each operation.
# =============================================================================

# An empty ledger carrying the tracked file's header only: fixtures never inherit live rows
# (the live ledger is seeded in the main checkout).
empty_ledger(){ { sed '/^schema_version:/,$d' "$1"; printf 'schema_version: 1\ndecisions: []\n'; } > "$2"; }

setup() {
  BATS_TEST_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
  REPO="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
  command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "jq not installed"
  command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || skip "yq not installed"
  [[ "$(yq --version 2>&1)" == *mikefarah*"version v4."* ]] || skip "Mike Farah yq v4 not installed"
  unset CLAUDE_SESSION_ID CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID LOA_UNATTENDED LOA_FLATLINE_MODE CI GITHUB_ACTIONS \
        LOA_HOOK_CONTEXT LOA_DEC_NO_FLOCK LOA_DEC_LOCK_WAIT
  T="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/proj"
  mkdir -p "$T/.claude/scripts/lib" "$T/grimoires/loa"
  cp "$REPO/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh" "$T/.claude/scripts/lib/"
  cp "$REPO/.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh" "$REPO/.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh" "$T/.claude/scripts/"
  [[ -f "$REPO/.claude/scripts/pii-filter.sh" ]] && cp "$REPO/.claude/scripts/pii-filter.sh" "$T/.claude/scripts/"
  empty_ledger "$REPO/grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml" "$T/grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml"
  git -C "$T" init -q
  D="$T/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh"
  L="$T/grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml"
  F="$T/fixture.yaml"
  cp "$L" "$F"
  ALT='{"option":"keep sequential","rejected_because":"one question per turn is slow"}'
}

# Same transformation as the writer's san1() (kf-write-lib.sh's), used to state expected values.
DEC_ULB_RE="$(printf '\302[\200-\237]|\342\200[\250\251]')"
san1(){ printf '%s' "${1-}" | LC_ALL=C tr -d '\000-\010\013\014\016-\037\177' | LC_ALL=C tr '\t\n\r' '   ' | LC_ALL=C sed -E "s/${DEC_ULB_RE}/ /g"' ; s/  +/ /g; s/^ //; s/ $//'; }

# new_open FILE [extra args]  -> an open row
new_open(){ local f="$1"; shift; bash "$D" new --file "$f" --summary "an open question" --phase discovery --category scope --recorded-by plan-and-analyze --source "prd.md#fr-1" --quiet "$@"; }
# new_prop FILE [extra args]  -> a proposed row
new_prop(){ local f="$1"; shift; bash "$D" new --file "$f" --summary "rounds is the thorough default" --phase discovery --category scope --recorded-by plan-and-analyze --source "prd.md#e (D1)" --status proposed --decision "pacing rounds" --rationale "brief recommendation" --alternative-json "$ALT" --cycle cycle-128 --quiet "$@"; }
field(){ yq -o=json -I0 '.' "$1" | jq -r --arg id "$2" ".decisions[] | select(.id == \$id) | $3"; }
ids(){ yq -o=json -I0 '.' "$1" | jq -r '[.decisions[].id] | join(",")'; }
confirm_op(){ bash "$D" confirm --recorded-by decisions-command --evidence "cli:2026-10-13T12:00:00Z" --quiet "$@"; }
lockpath(){ # target -> the writer's lock path
  local abs; abs="$(cd "$(dirname "$1")" && pwd -P)/$(basename "$1")"
  # shellcheck source=/dev/null
  ( source "$REPO/.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh"; printf '%s/.run/.dec-write-%s.lock' "$(cd "$T" && pwd -P)" "$(printf '%s' "$abs" | sha256_portable | cut -c1-12)" )
}
# A PATH holding every command of the current PATH except $1 (the tool reads as absent).
path_without(){
  local tool="$1" d="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/pw-$1" p f b
  mkdir -p "$d"
  local IFS=:
  for p in $PATH; do
    [[ -d "$p" ]] || continue
    for f in "$p"/*; do b="${f##*/}"; [[ "$b" == "$tool" || -e "$d/$b" ]] && continue; ln -s "$f" "$d/$b" 2>/dev/null || true; done

+## Interview Modes
+
+The skill resolves `interview_mode` (`interview.mode`, overridden per skill by `interview.per_skill.<skill>`), `pacing` and the input styles in its Config Reading block. These tables say what each value does.
+
+### Mode Behavior Table
+
+| Mode | Questions/Phase | Default pacing | Phase Gates | Gap Skipping |
+|---|---|---|---|---|
+| `thorough` | 3-6 (scales down with context) | `rounds` | All ON | Always ask `min_confirm` |
+| `minimal` | 1-2 | `batch` | `before_generation` only | Skip covered phases |
+
+An explicit `interview.pacing` wins over the mode default, so a config that sets `sequential` keeps it.
+
+### Input Style Resolution
+
+| Interaction Type | `structured` | `plain` |
+|---|---|---|
+| Routing gates | AskUserQuestion with options | "Continue, go back, or skip ahead?" |
+| Discovery questions | AskUserQuestion with suggested answers | Markdown question, user responds freely |

+
+## Question Pacing
+
+One key, `interview.pacing`, sets the pacing for the discovery interview, `/architect` Phase 2, `/sprint-plan` Phase 2 and `/chart`. Those skills point here.
+
+| Pacing | Behavior |
+|---|---|
+| `sequential` | Ask ONE question per turn. Wait for response. Then ask the next. The supported opt-out from rounds. |
+| `batch` | Present 3-6 numbered questions. User responds to all at once. The `minimal` default. |
+| `rounds` | Ask the whole frontier per turn, as below. The `thorough` default. |
+
+### Rounds
+
+1. **Frontier.** The frontier is every open question whose prerequisites are settled. A question that depends on another question still open waits for a later round. There is no cap on round size.
+2. **Facts stay out.** A fact (what code, reality files or docs say) is looked up, never asked; only decisions enter a round (Backpressure Protocol, "Fact or decision").
+3. **Phase scope.** A round runs within the current discovery phase. A question that belongs to a later phase is parked for that phase. Phase gates are unchanged.
+4. **Format.** Number questions across the session (`Q1`, `Q2`, ...), so ids never restart. Each question has a short title line starting `❓ Q<n>:`, the question worded so that "yes" accepts the recommendation, and a `➡ Recommended:` line giving the answer and its reason, with a citation when there is one. Close the round with the answer prompt and the comment block.
+5. **Answers.** A bare "yes" accepts every recommendation in the round. A numbered answer (`2: no, keep it local`) overrides that question. If the operator answers some numbers and not others, restate the unanswered ones with their recommendations and ask for confirmation; they take the recommendation only after the operator confirms. A question still unconfirmed is re-asked in the next round.
+6. **Recompute.** Before the next round, recompute the frontier from the answers: settled questions leave, questions whose prerequisites just settled join. "wrap up" ends the phase.
+7. **Comment block.** End every round with one HTML comment holding a JSON array, one object per question: `{"id": "Q4", "depends_on": ["Q1"]}`. `depends_on` lists the earlier questions this one needed settled, `[]` when none. A re-asked question keeps its id and carries `"reasked": true`. The block is how `tools/check-round-independence.sh` checks that no question in a round depends on another question in the same round.
+
+```
+Round 2 (Functional Requirements)
+
+❓ Q4: Ledger location
+Should the decision ledger live at grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml, tracked?
+➡ Recommended: yes (the spec and two readers already point there; decision-lineage.md:23)
+
+❓ Q5: Unattended record
+Should unattended runs write a DEC row for every decision they take for you?
+➡ Recommended: yes (makes "which did a human decide?" answerable)
+
+❓ Q2: Default pacing (re-asked)
+Should rounds be the default pacing for thorough mode?
+➡ Recommended: yes (one turn per frontier instead of one per question)
+
+"yes" accepts all three; answer by number to override one.
+<!-- round: 2; questions: [{"id":"Q4","depends_on":[]},{"id":"Q5","depends_on":["Q1"]},{"id":"Q2","depends_on":[],"reasked":true}] -->
+```
+
+The checker: `tools/check-round-independence.sh <transcript> [--min-average N] [--json]` exits 0 when every round is independent and the rounds average at least N questions (default 2; the final round is exempt when there are two or more rounds), 1 on a violation, 2 when the transcript has no round block.

+The skill resolves `interview_mode` (`interview.mode`, overridden per skill by `interview.per_skill.<skill>`), `pacing` and the input styles in its Config Reading block. These tables say what each value does.

+## Question Pacing
+
+One key, `interview.pacing`, sets the pacing for the discovery interview, `/architect` Phase 2, `/sprint-plan` Phase 2 and `/chart`. Those skills point here.
+
+| Pacing | Behavior |
+|---|---|
+| `sequential` | Ask ONE question per turn. Wait for response. Then ask the next. The supported opt-out from rounds. |
+| `batch` | Present 3-6 numbered questions. User responds to all at once. The `minimal` default. |
+| `rounds` | Ask the whole frontier per turn, as below. The `thorough` default. |
+
+### Rounds
+
+1. **Frontier.** The frontier is every open question whose prerequisites are settled. A question that depends on another question still open waits for a later round. There is no cap on round size.
+2. **Facts stay out.** A fact (what code, reality files or docs say) is looked up, never asked; only decisions enter a round (Backpressure Protocol, "Fact or decision").
+3. **Phase scope.** A round runs within the current discovery phase. A question that belongs to a later phase is parked for that phase. Phase gates are unchanged.
+4. **Format.** Number questions across the session (`Q1`, `Q2`, ...), so ids never restart. Each question has a short title line starting `❓ Q<n>:`, the question worded so that "yes" accepts the recommendation, and a `➡ Recommended:` line giving the answer and its reason, with a citation when there is one. Close the round with the answer prompt and the comment block.
+5. **Answers.** A bare "yes" accepts every recommendation in the round. A numbered answer (`2: no, keep it local`) overrides that question. If the operator answers some numbers and not others, restate the unanswered ones with their recommendations and ask for confirmation; they take the recommendation only after the operator confirms. A question still unconfirmed is re-asked in the next round.
+6. **Recompute.** Before the next round, recompute the frontier from the answers: settled questions leave, questions whose prerequisites just settled join. "wrap up" ends the phase.
+7. **Comment block.** End every round with one HTML comment holding a JSON array, one object per question: `{"id": "Q4", "depends_on": ["Q1"]}`. `depends_on` lists the earlier questions this one needed settled, `[]` when none. A re-asked question keeps its id and carries `"reasked": true`. The block is how `tools/check-round-independence.sh` checks that no question in a round depends on another question in the same round.

+➡ Recommended: yes (the spec and two readers already point there; decision-lineage.md:23)

+➡ Recommended: yes (one turn per frontier instead of one per question)

#!/usr/bin/env bats
# =============================================================================
# user-invoked-commands.bats: the operator-only command allowlist (FR-8, D-8.3)
# =============================================================================
# `.claude/data/user-invoked-commands.txt` lists commands carrying
# `disable-model-invocation: true`. The harness refuses those to the Skill
# tool (tests/unit/user-invoked-harness.bats), so no other command or skill
# body may tell the model to run one as a step. Asserts:
#   1. every listed command file exists and carries the flag
#   2. no other body has an operative line for a listed name
#   3. every command file carrying the flag is listed
#   4. no SKILL.md allowed-tools grants dec-write-lib.sh confirm, supersede
#      or context --clear (those are reachable only through /decisions)
# Each check is a function over a root directory, proved against fixtures.

setup() {
    PROJECT_ROOT="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
    export LC_ALL=C
}

# list_names <root>: the allowlisted names, comments and blanks stripped
list_names() {
    sed -e 's/#.*$//' -e 's/[[:space:]]*$//' -e 's/^[[:space:]]*//' \
        "$1/.claude/data/user-invoked-commands.txt" | grep -v '^$' || true
}

# frontmatter <file>: the first YAML frontmatter block (empty when none)
frontmatter() {
    awk 'NR==1 && $0!="---"{exit} /^---[[:space:]]*$/{n++; if(n==2) exit; next} n==1{print}' "$1"
}

has_flag() {
    frontmatter "$1" | grep -Eq '^disable-model-invocation:[[:space:]]*"?true"?[[:space:]]*$'
}

# check_listed_flagged <root>: prints each listed name whose file is missing or unflagged
check_listed_flagged() {
    local root="$1" name f
    while IFS= read -r name; do
        f="$root/.claude/commands/$name.md"
        if [[ ! -f "$f" ]]; then
            echo "missing: $name"
        elif ! has_flag "$f"; then
            echo "unflagged: $name"
        fi
    done < <(list_names "$root")
}

# check_flagged_listed <root>: prints each flagged command file not in the list
check_flagged_listed() {
    local root="$1" f name names
    names="$(list_names "$root")"
    for f in "$root"/.claude/commands/*.md; do
        [[ -f "$f" ]] || continue
        has_flag "$f" || continue
        name="$(basename "$f" .md)"
        grep -qxF "$name" <<<"$names" || echo "unlisted: $name"
    done
}

# check_operative <root>: prints file:line for each operative reference to a
# listed name in a body other than that command's own file
check_operative() {
    local root="$1" name re exempt
    exempt='(^|[^[:alpha:]])(user|operator|human|manually|suggest|recommend|tell|ask)'
    while IFS= read -r name; do
        # SDD D-8.3 pattern, widened: verbs match in any case and may take
        # "the" ("execute /x", "Invoke the /x skill").
        re="([Ee][Xx][Ee][Cc][Uu][Tt][Ee]|[Ii][Nn][Vv][Oo][Kk][Ee]|[Rr][Uu][Nn]|[Cc][Aa][Ll][Ll])[[:space:]]+(the[[:space:]]+)?\`?/${name}([^[:alnum:]_-]|\$)|Skill\\(.*${name}"
        { find "$root/.claude/commands" -name '*.md' -type f 2>/dev/null
          find "$root/.claude/skills" -name '*.md' -type f 2>/dev/null; } |
        while IFS= read -r f; do
            [[ "$f" == "$root/.claude/commands/$name.md" ]] && continue
            grep -nE "$re" "$f" 2>/dev/null | grep -viE "$exempt" |
                sed "s|^|${f#"$root"/}:|" || true
        done
    done < <(list_names "$root")
}

# check_operator_ops <root>: prints SKILL.md files whose allowed-tools grant
# an operator-only dec-write-lib.sh operation
check_operator_ops() {
    local root="$1" f
    while IFS= read -r f; do
        frontmatter "$f" | awk '/^allowed-tools:/{on=1; print; next} on && /^[[:space:]]+-|^[[:space:]]+[^[:space:]]/{print; next} {on=0}' |
            grep -Eq 'dec-write-lib\.sh[^,)]*(confirm|supersede|context[[:space:]]+--clear)' && echo "${f#"$root"/}"
    done < <(find "$root/.claude/skills" -name SKILL.md -type f 2>/dev/null)
    return 0
}

make_fixture() {
    local r="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR/fx"
    mkdir -p "$r/.claude/data" "$r/.claude/commands" "$r/.claude/skills/demo"
    printf 'alpha   # reason\n\n# comment\nbeta\n' > "$r/.claude/data/user-invoked-commands.txt"
    printf -- '---\nname: alpha\ndisable-model-invocation: true\n---\nbody\n' > "$r/.claude/commands/alpha.md"
    printf -- '---\nname: beta\ndisable-model-invocation: true\n---\nRun `/alpha` from another command body.\n' > "$r/.claude/commands/beta.md"
    printf -- '---\nname: demo\nallowed-tools: Read, Grep\n---\nTell the user to Run /alpha when ready.\n' > "$r/.claude/skills/demo/SKILL.md"
    echo "$r"
}

head/.gitignore:150 — The negation re-includes `grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml` as tracked team state, but the PR never adds that seed ledger. The diff has 38 files; the description says 39 are in scope. Without the file, every live-ledger write in the main checkout dies at dec-write-lib.sh:271 ("ledger not found ... restore the tracked grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml"). The setup of every test in tests/unit/dec-write-lib.bats (line 28) and the decisions fixtures in grimoire-index.bats:80 and validate-artifact.bats:630 build from `$REPO/grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml`, so they fail with "sed: can't read". With the hook enabled, every session gets the "unreadable" warning. Reproduced: all 44 dec-write-lib tests fail in setup without the file and pass once a seed with the expected header is added.
head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:513 — `op_confirm` calls `derive_attribution 0`, which throws away `--answer-ref` whenever `is_unattended` is true. That includes the non-live `prd` signal (ctx_signals line 178: a `**Status:**` line in grimoires/loa/prd.md containing "autonomous" or "unattended"). Confirm only refuses on *live* signals (line 509), so it goes ahead and records `decided_by: agent`, `decided_by_ref: null` for a decision the operator just confirmed through /decisions. Reproduced: with a PRD reading `**Status:** autonomous draft`, `confirm --recorded-by decisions-command --answer-ref cli:...` gives ["decided","agent",null]. The operator's decision is mis-attributed for good (append-only), and every `--not-decided-by operator` / `--voice agent,...` rendering then lists it as taken on the operator's behalf. The same signal makes operator reject/supersede of a decided row die or fall to the agent path (lines 572, 575, 600, 606).
head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:580 — `op_reject` of an agent-proposed replacement row leaves `supersede_proposed_by` on the old decided row pointing at the rejected row. The append-only check (validate-artifact.sh, the supersede_proposed_by rule) forbids ever clearing it, and `op_supersede` (line 601) refuses new non-operator proposals while it is set. So after one rejected replacement, agents can never propose another supersede of that decision. Reproduced: supersede DEC-0001 → DEC-0002, reject DEC-0002, then a second supersede fails with "a replacement is already proposed for DEC-0001: DEC-0002".
head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:606 — The operator `supersede` path moves the old decided row to `superseded` right away, while the replacement only lands `proposed`. If the operator then rejects the replacement (decisions.md:107 offers the confirm as optional), the ledger holds no decided row for that decision, and `superseded` is terminal, so it can't be restored. Reproduced: DEC-0001 superseded, DEC-0003 (its replacement) rejected. The old row should move only when the replacement is confirmed, as the agent path already does at line 545.
head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:359 — `is_operator_call` only checks that the caller passed the string `--recorded-by decisions-command`. Any agent Bash call can therefore run `confirm`, reject/supersede decided rows, or `context --clear` on its own proposals in an interactive session. `disable-model-invocation` on /decisions only blocks the Skill tool, and the bats checks only grep other command/skill bodies for the literal string. The PR's central claim that "the model cannot" confirm its own decisions (decisions.md:3, decisions.md:27) is not enforced. At minimum, document this as advisory, or bind confirm to something the model cannot forge (e.g. an operator-typed nonce or a TTY check).
head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:250 — With `--file`, `resolve_target` returns before the `ci_blocked` refusal and the worktree→pending redirect, whatever the path is. `--file grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml` therefore writes the live ledger from CI, GITHUB_ACTIONS or LOA_HOOK_CONTEXT=1, and from a linked worktree. The header (line 23) says only fixtures are exempt; the guard should reject a `--file` that resolves to the live ledger.
head/.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh:852 — `tolower(c[st]) ~ /resolved/` also matches "Unresolved" (and the template placeholder "Open/Resolved"), so open questions with no DEC id get the "Resolved without a DEC id" warning. Reproduced with a `| q | me | d | Unresolved | |` row. Match the cell exactly (trimmed, == "resolved") instead.
head/.claude/skills/run-mode/resources/render-templates.md:104 — `jq -r '.active_cycle'` prints the literal `null` when the key is absent, so step 2 runs `list --cycle null`. That matches no row, and step 4 then emits "_None: every decision in this run was the operator's._", the exact false claim step 3 is written to avoid. Use `// empty` and treat an empty cycle as "ledger unavailable".
Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED

head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:359 — `is_operator_call` only checks that the caller passed the string `--recorded-by decisions-command`. Any agent Bash call can therefore run `confirm`, reject/supersede decided rows, or `context --clear` on its own proposals in an interactive session. `disable-model-invocation` on /decisions only blocks the Skill tool, and the bats checks only grep other command/skill bodies for the literal string. The PR's central claim that "the model cannot" confirm its own decisions (decisions.md:3, decisions.md:27) is not enforced. At minimum, document this as advisory, or bind confirm to something the model cannot forge (e.g. an operator-typed nonce or a TTY check).
head/.claude/scripts/lib/dec-write-lib.sh:250 — With `--file`, `resolve_target` returns before the `ci_blocked` refusal and the worktree→pending redirect, whatever the path is. `--file grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml` therefore writes the live ledger from CI, GITHUB_ACTIONS or LOA_HOOK_CONTEXT=1, and from a linked worktree. The header (line 23) says only fixtures are exempt; the guard should reject a `--file` that resolves to the live ledger.
head/.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh:852 — `tolower(c[st]) ~ /resolved/` also matches "Unresolved" (and the template placeholder "Open/Resolved"), so open questions with no DEC id get the "Resolved without a DEC id" warning. Reproduced with a `| q | me | d | Unresolved | |` row. Match the cell exactly (trimmed, == "resolved") instead.
head/.claude/skills/run-mode/resources/render-templates.md:104 — `jq -r '.active_cycle'` prints the literal `null` when the key is absent, so step 2 runs `list --cycle null`. That matches no row, and step 4 then emits "_None: every decision in this run was the operator's._", the exact false claim step 3 is written to avoid. Use `// empty` and treat an empty cycle as "ledger unavailable".
Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED

The verdict is **CHANGES_REQUIRED**. The review, with eight findings, is in `/workspace/review.md`. I confirmed the first five by running them against a scratch copy of the head files; none of the files under `pr/` were changed.

**Blocking:**
1. **The ledger file is missing.** The `.gitignore` change (line 150) starts tracking `grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml`, but the PR never adds the file. The description says 39 files and the diff has 38. Without it, the writer refuses every write to the shared ledger in the main checkout, and all 44 `dec-write-lib.bats` tests fail during setup. Once I added a stub ledger, all 44 passed.
2. **Operator confirmations get recorded as agent decisions.** If `prd.md` has a status line saying "autonomous", the confirm step throws away the operator's answer reference and records `decided_by: agent` (`dec-write-lib.sh:513`). Rows can only be added to, never edited, so the wrong attribution is permanent.
3. **One rejected replacement blocks future ones.** When a proposed replacement is rejected, the old row keeps pointing at it, and the validator never allows that pointer to be cleared. After that, agents can't propose another replacement for that decision (`:580`).
4. **The operator path for replacing a decision can lose it.** It marks the old row superseded straight away, while the new row is only proposed. If the operator then rejects the new row, nothing decided is left for that decision, and it can't be restored (`:606`).
5. **"The model cannot confirm its own decisions" isn't enforced.** The operator check only looks for the text `--recorded-by decisions-command`, which any agent shell command can pass. Blocking `/decisions` from the model's Skill tool doesn't stop the model from running the script directly (`:359`).

**Lesser:**
6. **The file-override option skips the safety checks.** Passing the shared ledger's own path with `--file` lets a write through from CI, a hook or a linked worktree (`:250`).
7. **"Unresolved" counts as "Resolved" in the SDD check.** The Open Questions check matches the substring, so unresolved rows trigger the missing-DEC warning (`validate-artifact.sh:852`).
8. **A missing cycle id gives a false "operator decided everything".** The PR-body step reads `active_cycle` without a fallback, so a missing value becomes the literal `null`. Nothing matches, and the section then claims every decision was the operator's (`render-templates.md:104`).

The round-independence checker passes all 13 of its tests. The tests for validate-artifact (51) and the operator-only harness (5) also passed. Several other suites (the session-start hook, the command allowlist, agents-md-gen, two grimoire-index tests) couldn't run fully here because they depend on repo files that aren't part of the PR, so those were checked by reading only.
